PT-porto.why: Port wine cellars along the Douro and an old town that climbs up from the river.

ES-barcelona.why: Gaudí's buildings, a city beach and late nights in one city.
ES-barcelona.level_note: More expensive than the Spanish average, especially accommodation.

ES-madrid.why: The Prado, tapas bars and a city life that starts late.

ES-sevilla.why: The Alcázar, orange trees and flamenco. Summer is very hot, so spring and autumn are the time to go.
ES-sevilla.name: Seville

ES-valencia.why: The home of paella, with a city beach, a park in an old riverbed and fewer tourists than Barcelona.

ES-malaga.why: Picasso's birthplace, with a beach, museums and mild winters.

ES-san-sebastian.why: A shell-shaped city beach and bars full of pintxos in the Basque Country.
ES-san-sebastian.level_note: More expensive than the Spanish average, especially food and accommodation.

ES-granada.why: The Alhambra above the city and the Sierra Nevada in the background.

FR-paris.why: Museums, cafés and boulevards: the city most others are compared with.

FR-nice.why: The largest city on the Riviera, with a seafront promenade, an old town and trains along the coast to Monaco.

FR-menton.why: A pastel-coloured old town by the Italian border, on the same stretch of coast as Monaco but at a slower pace.

FR-lyon.why: France's food capital, with bouchons and an old quarter between two rivers.
FR-lyon.level_note: Our judgement: cheaper than Paris and the Riviera, which pull up France's average.

FR-bordeaux.why: A wine city with 18th-century quays along the Garonne and vineyards around the corner.
FR-bordeaux.level_note: Our judgement: cheaper than Paris and the Riviera, which pull up France's average.

FR-strasbourg.why: Half-timbered houses and canals in Alsace, and one of Europe's oldest Christmas markets.
FR-strasbourg.level_note: Our judgement. The Post Office ranks the city as one of Western Europe's cheapest city breaks in 2026.

FR-lille.why: Flemish façades and a large art museum, close to the Belgian border.
FR-lille.level_note: Our judgement. The Post Office ranks the city as one of Western Europe's cheapest city breaks in 2026.

IT-rom.why: The Colosseum, the Pantheon and the Vatican within walking distance of each other.
IT-rom.name: Rome

IT-florens.why: The city of the Renaissance, with the Uffizi and the cathedral in the middle of Tuscany.
IT-florens.name: Florence

IT-venedig.why: A city without cars, built on islands in a lagoon.
IT-venedig.name: Venice
IT-venedig.level_note: More expensive than the Italian average, especially accommodation and food near the canals.

IT-neapel.why: The home of pizza, with Pompeii and Vesuvius within reach.
IT-neapel.name: Naples
IT-neapel.level_note: Our judgement: southern Italy is cheaper than the national average.

IT-bologna.why: Arcades, towers and a cuisine the rest of Italy looks up to.

IT-palermo.why: Markets, street food and Arab-Norman churches in Sicily.
IT-palermo.level_note: Our judgement: southern Italy is cheaper than the national average.

IT-sanremo.why: The Italian Riviera's city of flowers, with a casino, palm trees and an old quarter on the hill.

IT-trieste.why: A port city with Habsburg palaces and old coffee houses, in the corner by Slovenia.

IT-lecce.why: A baroque city in sandstone at the far end of Puglia, with beaches on two seas.
IT-lecce.level_note: Our judgement: southern Italy is cheaper than the national average.

BE-bryssel.why: The Grand-Place, art nouveau, waffles and beer.
BE-bryssel.name: Brussels

BE-gent.why: Medieval quays and a castle in the middle of a lively student city.
BE-gent.name: Ghent

NL-rotterdam.why: Modern architecture, a market hall and Europe's largest port.

NL-utrecht.why: Canals with two-level quays and cafés down by the water.

DE-munchen.why: Beer halls, parks and the Alps within a day trip.
DE-munchen.name: Munich
DE-munchen.level_note: Our judgement: one of Germany's most expensive cities.

DE-hamburg.why: A port city with brick warehouse districts and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall.

DE-leipzig.why: Bach's city, with a big cultural scene in old industrial districts.

AT-wien.why: Imperial palaces, concert halls and coffee houses with newspapers on sticks.
AT-wien.name: Vienna

AT-salzburg.why: Mozart's birthplace, with a baroque old town below a fortress.

AT-graz.why: Austria's second-largest city, with red roofs, a clock tower on the hill and vineyards to the south.
AT-graz.level_note: Our judgement: cheaper than Vienna and Salzburg.

CH-zurich.why: An old town by a lake where people swim in summer, with the Alps as a backdrop.
CH-zurich.name: Zurich

CH-geneve.why: A lakeside city with a fountain and views of Mont Blanc.
CH-geneve.name: Geneva

CZ-prag.why: Charles Bridge, the castle and an old town that survived the war.
CZ-prag.name: Prague

CZ-brno.why: The Czech Republic's second city, with functionalist villas, wine bars and few tourists.

PL-krakow.why: One of Europe's largest medieval squares and the royal castle of Wawel.
PL-krakow.name: Kraków

PL-wroclaw.why: A colourful square, islands in the river Oder and small bronze dwarfs all over the city.

HU-budapest.why: Thermal baths, ruin bars and the parliament by the Danube.

SK-bratislava.why: A small capital on the Danube with a castle on the hill, an hour from Vienna.

SI-ljubljana.why: A car-free centre along a river, with a castle on the hill and the mountains close by.

SI-piran.why: A Venetian small town on a headland in the Adriatic.

HR-rovinj.why: A fishing town on a peninsula in Istria, with alleys leading up to the church.

HR-zadar.why: Roman ruins, a sea organ played by the waves and islands offshore.

EE-tallinn.why: A medieval town with walls and towers, a ferry ride from Helsinki.

LV-riga.why: Art nouveau façades, market halls in old zeppelin hangars and an old town.

LT-vilnius.why: A baroque old town and the artists' quarter of Užupis.

BA-sarajevo.why: An Ottoman bazaar and Austro-Hungarian quarters side by side, surrounded by mountains.

BA-mostar.why: The stone bridge Stari Most over an emerald-green river.

RS-belgrad.why: A fortress where the Sava meets the Danube, and nightlife on boats along the river.
RS-belgrad.name: Belgrade

AL-tirana.why: A colourful capital with café culture, bunkers turned into museums and a mountain with a cable car.

ME-kotor.why: A walled town at the innermost end of a fjord-like bay, with steep mountains rising straight up.

MK-ohrid.why: An old town with Byzantine churches by one of Europe's oldest lakes.

BG-sofia.why: Cathedrals, Roman ruins in the metro and Mount Vitosha at the city limits.

BG-plovdiv.why: One of Europe's oldest cities, with a Roman theatre and painted wooden houses.

RO-bukarest.why: Wide boulevards, an enormous parliament palace and an old quarter full of bars.
RO-bukarest.name: Bucharest

RO-brasov.why: A Saxon town in the Carpathians, with castles and mountain trails all around.

GR-thessaloniki.why: Greece's second city, with a seafront promenade, Byzantine churches and a reputation for the country's best food.

GR-nafplio.why: A harbour town with Venetian fortresses in the Peloponnese, close to Mycenae and Epidaurus.

GR-rhodos.why: The medieval city of the Knights inside the walls, with beaches outside.
GR-rhodos.name: Rhodes Town

MT-valletta.why: A fortified capital in honey-coloured stone, surrounded by sea on three sides.

IE-dublin.why: Pubs with live music, Georgian quarters and Trinity College.

SE-goteborg.why: Canals, seafood and an archipelago reached by tram and ferry.
SE-goteborg.name: Gothenburg
SE-goteborg.level_note: Our judgement, the same level as we set for Stockholm.

NO-bergen.why: The Hanseatic wharf Bryggen between seven mountains, and the gateway to the fjords.

DK-arhus.why: Denmark's second city, with the ARoS art museum, the open-air museum Den Gamle By and harbour baths.
DK-arhus.name: Aarhus

JP-tokyo.why: The world's largest metropolitan area, where neon, temples and tiny six-seat bars share the same block.
JP-tokyo.level_note: Our judgement: the yen has lost a lot of value since the index was measured in 2021, so Japan is cheaper for visitors today.

JP-kyoto.why: Japan's old imperial capital, with temples, gardens and the geisha district of Gion.
JP-kyoto.level_note: Our judgement: the yen has lost a lot of value since the index was measured in 2021, so Japan is cheaper for visitors today.

JP-kanazawa.why: Kenrokuen garden, samurai quarters and a fish market, without Kyoto's crowds.
JP-kanazawa.level_note: Our judgement: the yen has lost a lot of value since the index was measured in 2021, so Japan is cheaper for visitors today.

KR-seoul.why: Royal palaces between skyscrapers, street food and nightlife that never closes.

KR-busan.why: South Korea's port city, with city beaches, a fish market and a temple by the sea.

TW-taipei.why: Night markets, tea houses and hiking trails that start where the metro ends.

HK-hongkong.why: Skyscrapers between mountains and sea, with dim sum and a ferry across the harbour.
HK-hongkong.name: Hong Kong
HK-hongkong.level_note: Our judgement: accommodation is expensive for visitors.

SG-singapore.why: A city-state with hawker centres, gardens and four cuisines on the same street.
SG-singapore.level_note: Our judgement: hotels and alcohol are expensive for visitors, even though street food is cheap.

TH-bangkok.why: Temples, canals and street food in one of Asia's most intense cities.

TH-chiang-mai.why: An old town inside a moat in northern Thailand, with hundreds of temples and the mountains close by.

TH-krabi.why: Limestone cliffs rising straight out of the sea and boats out to the islands.

VN-hanoi.why: Narrow old quarters, lakes and noodle soup on a plastic stool.

VN-hoi-an.why: An old trading town with lanterns, tailors and a beach within cycling distance.

VN-ho-chi-minh.why: Vietnam's largest city, with mopeds, markets and war history.
VN-ho-chi-minh.name: Ho Chi Minh City

KH-siem-reap.why: The town next to Angkor Wat and the other temples of the Khmer empire.

LA-luang-prabang.why: A temple town where the Mekong meets a tributary, with waterfalls outside town.

ID-ubud.why: Bali's cultural centre, surrounded by rice terraces and temples.

ID-yogyakarta.why: Java's cultural centre, with the temples of Borobudur and Prambanan within reach.

MY-kuala-lumpur.why: Twin towers, food markets and Malay, Chinese and Indian cooking side by side.

MY-george-town.why: Penang's old town, known for street food, street art and shophouses.

PH-el-nido.why: Lagoons and limestone islands on Palawan, explored by boat.

IN-jaipur.why: The Pink City of Rajasthan, with palaces and Amber Fort.

IN-kochi.why: A port city in Kerala with Chinese fishing nets, the spice trade and canals to the south.

LK-galle.why: A Dutch fort on a headland in southern Sri Lanka, with beaches all around.

NP-katmandu.why: Temple squares and stupas in a valley below the Himalayas, and the starting point for treks.
NP-katmandu.name: Kathmandu

AE-dubai.why: Skyscrapers, shopping malls and beach in the desert.
AE-dubai.level_note: Our judgement: hotels, restaurants and alcohol are expensive for visitors.

OM-muskat.why: A low white capital between mountains and sea, with a souk, forts and wadis outside town.
OM-muskat.name: Muscat

JO-petra.why: The town by Petra, the rock city the Nabataeans carved out of pink sandstone.

GE-tbilisi.why: Wooden balconies, sulphur baths and one of the world's oldest wine countries around the corner.

AM-jerevan.why: Pink tuff stone, cafés and views of Mount Ararat.
AM-jerevan.name: Yerevan

UZ-samarkand.why: The Silk Road city, with Registan square and blue tiled domes.

TR-antalya.why: An old harbour town on the Turkish Riviera, with beaches and ancient ruins nearby.

TR-goreme.why: A village in the middle of Cappadocia, with rock formations, cave churches and hot-air balloons at dawn.

MA-marrakech.why: Souks, riads and Jemaa el-Fna square, with the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.

MA-chefchaouen.why: A blue-painted mountain town in the Rif.

MA-essaouira.why: A windy harbour town with white walls by the Atlantic, calmer than Marrakech.

EG-kairo.why: The pyramids of Giza on the edge of one of Africa's largest cities.
EG-kairo.name: Cairo

EG-luxor.why: Karnak, Luxor Temple and the Valley of the Kings on either side of the Nile.

TN-tunis.why: The medina, the mosaics of the Bardo Museum and the ruins of Carthage in a suburb.

ZA-kapstaden.why: Table Mountain above the city, beaches on two oceans and vineyards a short drive away.
ZA-kapstaden.name: Cape Town

TZ-zanzibar.why: Zanzibar's old stone town, with carved doors, a spice market and beaches around the island.
TZ-zanzibar.level_note: Our judgement: the island is more expensive for visitors than the Tanzanian average.

NA-swakopmund.why: A coastal town with German colonial architecture where the dunes of the Namib meet the Atlantic.

US-san-francisco.why: Hills, cable cars and the Golden Gate Bridge by a foggy bay.
US-san-francisco.level_note: Our judgement, the same level as we set for New York.

US-new-orleans.why: The birthplace of jazz, with the French Quarter and Creole cooking.

US-chicago.why: The home of the skyscraper on Lake Michigan, with blues and deep-dish pizza.

US-savannah.why: A Southern city with squares on a grid, oaks draped in Spanish moss and old wooden houses.

CA-vancouver.why: A big city between sea and mountains, with rainforest in the city park.

CA-quebec.why: A French-speaking city with a city wall and old quarters above the Saint Lawrence River.
CA-quebec.name: Quebec City

CA-montreal.why: A French-speaking metropolis with festivals all summer and bagels around the clock.
CA-montreal.name: Montreal

MX-mexico-city.why: A giant city at high altitude, with Aztec ruins, murals and tacos on every corner.

MX-oaxaca.why: Mexico's food city, with mole, mezcal and the ruined city of Monte Albán above.

MX-merida.why: A colonial capital on the Yucatán, close to Maya ruins and cenotes.

CR-la-fortuna.why: A small town by the Arenal volcano, with hot springs, rainforest and hanging bridges.

GT-antigua.why: A colonial town with cobbled streets, surrounded by three volcanoes.

PA-panama.why: Skyscrapers, the old town Casco Viejo and ships on their way through the canal.

CO-cartagena.why: A walled colonial city on the Caribbean, in strong colours.

CO-medellin.why: A big city in a green valley, with cable cars up to the hillside neighbourhoods.

PE-cusco.why: The capital of the Inca empire in the Andes, and the gateway to Machu Picchu.

PE-lima.why: South America's food capital, on cliffs above the Pacific.

EC-quito.why: A high-altitude capital in the Andes, with a large colonial centre, almost on the equator.

CL-valparaiso.why: A port city on steep hills, with funiculars, street art and colourful houses.

AR-buenos-aires.why: Tango, grilled meat and wide avenues.
AR-buenos-aires.level_note: Our judgement: prices have risen sharply since the index was measured in 2021.

BR-rio.why: Beaches, Sugarloaf Mountain and the Christ statue in a city squeezed between mountains and sea.

BR-salvador.why: Brazil's first capital, with colourful colonial quarters and Afro-Brazilian music.

UY-colonia.why: A Portuguese colonial small town on the Río de la Plata, a ferry ride from Buenos Aires.

AU-melbourne.why: Coffee, laneways with street art and trams.

AU-hobart.why: Tasmania's capital, with the MONA art museum, a Saturday market and wilderness close by.

AU-cairns.why: The base for the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree rainforest.

NZ-queenstown.why: A small town by a lake between mountains, known for adventure sports.

NZ-wellington.why: A compact capital on a bay, with the national museum Te Papa and a cable car up to the view.

FJ-nadi.why: Fiji's gateway to the Mamanuca and Yasawa island groups.

MC-monaco.why: A principality of two square kilometres, with a casino, superyachts and Formula 1 on the streets.

DK-kopenhamn.why: A cycling city with canals, Tivoli and one of the best food scenes in the Nordics.

NO-oslo.why: A capital between fjord and forest, with the Opera House, the Munch Museum and swimming in the city centre.

NL-amsterdam.why: Canals, bicycles and museums such as the Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum.

DE-berlin.why: History on every block, major museums and nightlife that runs until morning.

SE-stockholm.why: A capital on fourteen islands, with the Old Town, the Vasa Museum and the archipelago beyond.

FI-helsingfors.why: Design, saunas by the sea and the sea fortress of Suomenlinna a short ferry ride away.

IS-reykjavik.why: A small capital and the base for waterfalls, geysers, hot pools and northern lights.

GR-aten.why: The Acropolis above a messy, lively city with tavernas in every alley.

HR-dubrovnik.why: A walled city on the Adriatic, with ramparts to walk and swimming from the rocks.

HR-split.why: A city built inside a Roman emperor's palace, with ferries out to the islands.

HR-zagreb.why: Café life, the upper town with its funicular and a big Christmas market in December.

TR-istanbul.why: A city on two continents, with Hagia Sophia, bazaars and ferries across the Bosphorus.

US-new-york.why: Skyscrapers, Central Park, museums and a city that stays open around the clock.

AU-sydney.why: The Opera House and Harbour Bridge by the harbour, with surf beaches a bus ride away.

PL-gdansk.why: A Hanseatic city on the Baltic, with gabled houses, amber and sandy beaches not far away.

PT-lissabon.why: Hills, tiles and trams at the mouth of the Tagus, with the Atlantic coast a short train ride away.
